"Allegedly" is doing a lot of work here. Binance hasn't said anything yet.

hits.hook: Legendary investor Stanley Druckenmiller says America's real debt is closer to $200 trillion once you count the Social Security and Medicare promised to future retirees.
hits.draft_en:
Druckenmiller: US 'real debt' is closer to $200T once you count promised Social Security and Medicare.

That's not the same as Treasury debt.
- one is a legal obligation
- the other is a promise that can be cut, taxed or delayed
- both get paid in dollars someone can create

For a $BTC spot holder, the question isn't the headline number. It's how the gap gets closed.

Higher taxes, cuts, or inflation: which one do you think wins?
Repost if you want more people asking this.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Important distinction: Treasury debt is a contract, entitlement promises are policy.

The $200T figure matters less than how the gap closes: cuts, taxes, or inflation. Only one of those is a direct argument for $BTC.
hits.video_tip: Two stacked bars, 'Treasury debt' vs 'promised benefits', then three arrows: cuts, taxes, inflation; 8s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Separate legal debt from unfunded promises and ask which path closes the gap (cuts, taxes, inflation); suggest checking the trustees' report for the 2032 date.
hits.why_chosen: Big fiscal number with 28 replies; room to separate contract from promise and tie it to $BTC without hype.

hits.name: Anthony Pompliano 🌪
hits.text: People are working harder in an age of AI because your work capacity expands to fill the available time.
hits.hook: People are working harder in an age of AI because your work capacity expands to fill the available time.
hits.draft_en:
"People work harder in the age of AI."

Maybe. Or they just fill the extra time.

Same trap in markets:
- more charts, more indicators, more screen time
- more trades doesn't mean better returns
- for spot $BTC, a simple DCA rule often beats constant tinkering

Tools that save time only help if you stop using the saved time to fidget.

Has AI made you trade more or less?
If this was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Parkinson's law with better tools.

The real question is output, not hours. Is anyone measuring whether the extra work produces more, or just more activity?
hits.video_tip: Clock speeding up while a to-do list keeps growing, then cut to a single 'DCA' rule card; 6s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Frame it as Parkinson's law and ask whether output rose or only activity did; bridge to overtrading vs. simple rules in BTC.
hits.why_chosen: Debatable one-line claim with 51 replies; bridges to activity vs. results in investing.

"30K qubits could crack Bitcoin keys in one hour."

Before panicking, separate three things:

- logical vs. physical qubits

Want me to go deeper on which coins are most exposed?
hits.draft_quote_en:
Key detail missing from the headline: 30K of which kind of qubits, and how far is today's hardware from that?

Also worth separating coins with exposed public keys from the rest. The risk isn't evenly spread.
hits.video_tip: Split screen: 'estimate' vs 'existing hardware', a gap bar between them labeled 'check the paper'; 8s, 9:16.
hits.reply_angle: Ask whether the 30K are logical or physical qubits and how that compares to current hardware; point to the share of BTC in addresses with exposed public keys as the real exposure check.
hits.why_chosen: Scary-number headline with no context; room for a clarifying question and a calm, data-minded caveat.

We can't name them, but we can see how long coins have sat unmoved. That's the part that matters for supply: how much is likely to ever hit the market?

hits.hook: As more and more of these schemes are uncovered, it makes one wonder just how much of the US government's $2 trillion deficit can be attributed to fraud. https://t.co/aNEndEZHN8
hits.draft_en:
A $2T deficit.

People love to blame it on fraud.
Some of it is. Most of it isn't.

The bigger driver is boring:
- interest on existing debt
- entitlements that grow on autopilot
- spending neither party cuts

Why I care as a $BTC holder:
Deficits don't get repaid. They get financed. That pressure shows up in the currency.

Fraud or structure: which one do you think moves the number more?
If this was useful, a repost helps more people see it.
hits.draft_quote_en:
Fraud is real, and it's easy outrage. But how much of $2T is it, really?

Interest on the debt alone is now one of the biggest lines in the budget (check CBO). Even if every scheme got caught, the structural gap stays.

hits.reply_angle: Ask for the split: compare known improper-payment estimates (check GAO) with net interest and entitlements in CBO's deficit breakdown; structure, not scandal, drives the number.

New phishing trick: emails that come from Google's own infrastructure.

Basic rules for anyone holding $BTC:

- type the address yourself
- seed words never go into a browser, ever

Boring rules beat clever attackers.

What's your one non-negotiable security rule?
Save this and send it to the person in your family who clicks links.

Good reminder that sender reputation isn't a security check anymore.

For anyone with BTC in a hot wallet or on an exchange: don't log in from email links, type the URL yourself, and use a hardware key for 2FA where you can.
